zh.title: IATA 發布新版客艙寵物運輸作業指南
zh.summary: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）發布新的機艙內寵物運輸作業指引，旨在建立業界最佳實務，協助航空公司制定一致性政策。該自願性指南涵蓋訂位、報到、登機、空中旅程及轉機等各階段，以因應旅客對寵物友善航空旅行日益增長的需求。
body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）於2026年7月31日發布了全新的《機艙內寵物運輸作業指南》，為航空公司提供從訂位、報到、登機、飛行過程到抵達的完整建議程序，以提升各航空公司間寵物政策的一致性。
IATA指出，此指南為自願性質，但隨著寵物友善航空旅行需求持續成長，該指引建立了業界最佳實務。根據IATA於2025年進行的全球旅客調查，約四分之一的旅客曾攜帶或考慮攜帶寵物旅行，但許多旅客認為航空公司規則不一致是主要的困擾來源。
該指南建議航空公司應發布明確的規範，包括各國進口限制、費用及預訂程序。同時，航空公司應要求旅客若計畫攜帶寵物旅行，必須事先通知。IATA也建議地勤人員應於報到時確認動物的健康狀況、獸醫證明與進口文件齊全、寵物能舒適地待在運輸籠內，且運輸籠符合航空公司要求。
在機上，IATA建議寵物運輸籠在滑行、起飛、降落及遭遇亂流期間應全程置於前方座椅下方，且動物在航程中須全程留在籠內。寵物不應占用旅客座椅，或阻礙走道與緊急出口。
對於轉機旅程，IATA鼓勵航空公司提供明確資訊，包括行程中每段航班是否都接受寵物、過境與目的地所需的文件要求、是否需要在轉機時領回並重新託運寵物，以及轉機機場內寵物活動區域的位置與使用限制等。
IATA全球貨運主管布倫丹·蘇利文表示：「寵物是深受摯愛的家庭成員。帶著寵物旅行的人們需要清晰的指引，來了解旅程中每個階段的預期情況。」他強調，準備充足的旅客和產業最佳實務，能讓航空公司為攜帶寵物的旅客提供安全、一致且有效率的體驗。

en.title: IATA Publishes New Operational Guidelines for Pets Traveling in Aircraft Cabins
en.summary: The International Air Transport Association has released new operational guidelines for in-cabin pet transport, aiming to establish industry best practices and help airlines develop consistent procedures. The voluntary guidance covers the entire journey, from booking and check-in through boarding, the in-flight experience, and arrival, addressing growing demand for pet-friendly air travel.
body: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) published new operational guidelines for airlines transporting pets in aircraft cabins on July 31, 2026, aiming to ensure greater consistency in pet policies which often vary widely between carriers. The new Operational Guidelines for In-Cabin Pet Transport provide airlines with recommended procedures covering every stage of the journey, from booking and check-in through boarding, the in-flight experience, and arrival.

The guidance is voluntary but establishes industry best practice as demand for pet-friendly air travel continues to grow. According to IATA’s 2025 Global Passenger Survey, around one in four passengers have travelled or would consider travelling with a pet. However, many cited inconsistent airline rules as a major source of confusion.

The document focuses specifically on animals accompanying passengers inside the aircraft cabin, unlike existing IATA Live Animals Regulations which address pets travelling in cargo holds. IATA recommends that airlines require advance notification if a passenger plans to travel with a pet.

IATA recommends that airline staff should verify the animal is healthy enough to travel, required veterinary and import documentation is complete, the pet fits comfortably inside its carrier, and the carrier complies with airline requirements. The guidelines also suggest staff visually assess whether an animal appears distressed or unfit for travel before boarding.

During the flight, IATA recommends carriers remain beneath the seat in front during taxi, take-off, landing and turbulence. Animals should remain inside the carrier throughout the flight and pets should never occupy passenger seats or obstruct aisles or emergency exits. Cabin crew should receive advance notification identifying passengers travelling with pets to manage seating arrangements.

For connecting flights, IATA recommends airlines give passengers clear information about transfer procedures before departure, including whether pets are accepted on every flight in the itinerary, documentation requirements, whether the pet must be reclaimed and rechecked during connections, and the availability of pet relief areas at connecting airports.
